clue.text: Men with no end of cash getting crowns

indicators.note: no means the chosen letter is dropped from the word for men

parts.note: chaps is an informal word for men

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of the word cash

explanation.surface: Men who have run out of money end up with crowns, perhaps dental ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Caps and crowns are both tops, and a dentist's crown is also called a cap.

clue.text: Offer incentives after prisoner's scorn

indicators.note: after puts the word for offering incentives behind the one for a prisoner

parts.note: con, short for convict, is a prisoner
to tempt is to offer incentives

explanation.surface: A prisoner is scornful when bribed with incentives.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt and scorn are synonyms for disdain.

clue.text: Rebuilt hip bistro must ignore small bar

indicators.note: rebuilt says the letters of hip bistro are put together again in a new order
must ignore says one letter is left out of the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A trendy refurbished bistro must disregard a little bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop S from HIPBISTRO and rearrange HIPBITRO.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to forbid it, a verb sense quite unlike the pub counter suggested.

clue.text: Back victory with Germany's renewed energy

parts.note: to back a proposal is to second it
a victory is a win
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A supporter cheers a German win that revives a flagging team.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a fresh burst of stamina after tiring, as runners feel midway through a race.

clue.text: English team lose, having no heart for enforced absence abroad

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football side

indicators.note: having no heart keeps only the outer letters of the word lose

explanation.surface: An English side loses heartlessly and is banished abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Being banished from one's homeland is a forced absence overseas.

clue.text: Miss alarm concerning student caught in leak

parts.note: over can mean concerning, as in a row over money

indicators.note: caught in says the learner's letter is trapped within the word for leaking

parts.note: to seep is to leak slowly
L for learner is a student driver

explanation.surface: A student caught in a leak misses an alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep past the time one intended to wake is to miss the morning alarm.

clue.text: Stevedores to cut rows about welcoming king and Queen

parts.note: to dock is to cut, as a tail or wages

indicators.note: welcoming says the shuffled letters take in king and queen
about says the letters of rows are turned around into a different order

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Royals are welcomed during a row over cuts at the port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but is the anagram signal, and 'to cut' is the verb for trimming a tail or wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevedores load and unload ships, so they are waterfront labourers.

clue.text: I drink after church freezes

indicators.note: after puts the drink behind the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drink after church and feels the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb for becoming coated with frost, as windscreens do in winter.

clue.text: Study suppressing on-target earnings is mean

indicators.note: in a down answer suppressing places the room word on top of the earnings abbreviation

parts.note: a den is a study or private room
OTE abbreviates on-target earnings in job adverts

explanation.surface: A study hiding one's sales bonuses is miserly.
explanation.definitionFit: To signify or indicate is a verb sense of mean.

clue.text: Time nobody finishes early?

indicators.note: finishes early says the word stops before its final letter

parts.note: nobody means no one

explanation.surface: A wry question about a time of day when no one gets to leave work early.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is a specific time of day, twelve o'clock.

clue.text: Sack vet — that's for keeping the temperature down

definitions.text: that's for keeping the temperature down

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
to vet candidates is to screen them

explanation.surface: Seems to be about dismissing a vet, then explains a device for cooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' and 'vet' look like nouns, a bag and an animal doctor, but both are verbs of employment.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel set before a hearth shields a room from the fire's heat, keeping things cooler nearby.

clue.text: Palestine ordered to release an ancient letter

indicators.note: the letters of Palestine are rearranged once the two letters of an are let go

explanation.surface: Instructions about freeing something from Palestine, with a nod to antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A and N out of PALESTINE and rearrange the remaining PLESTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament epistles are ancient letters written by apostles to early churches.

clue.text: Doctor may keep oath as reward for one's labour

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A doctor keeping the Hippocratic oath as a reward for work.
explanation.definitionFit: Net pay after deductions is what a worker actually receives for the job.

clue.text: What a carpenter may make of a good deal?

definitions.text: What a carpenter may make of a good deal?

parts.words: What a carpenter may make of a good deal
parts.note: a good deal suggests profit, but a carpenter cutting a deal (a plank of pine or fir) makes fine wood particles

explanation.surface: A tradesman making money from a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' is softwood timber; sawing it produces the dusty residue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawing timber leaves fine particles behind, the by-product a carpenter literally makes from deal wood.

clue.text: Report of couple likely to take offence producing fruit?

indicators.note: report signals that the words are heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a touchy couple would be a prickly pair

explanation.surface: A news report about a touchy couple that leads to some result.
explanation.definitionFit: The cactus Opuntia bears an edible spiny fruit known by this name.

clue.text: Rent subject to Sky — or new division in England

indicators.note: subject to places the renting word beneath the scrambled letters in a down answer
new asks for the letters of Sky and or in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: to rent is to hire

explanation.surface: A rent rise tied to Sky TV causes a split in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject to' means lying beneath: in a down answer the renting word sits under the shuffled letters marked by 'new'. Counties are the traditional divisions of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic county in northern England, a county being an administrative division.

clue.text: Reckon European nation must absorb one million

indicators.note: must absorb says the nation word takes the pair of letters inside it

parts.note: a state is a nation
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A European country having to take in a million migrants.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to calculate roughly, a synonym verb.

clue.text: The man's in a club that's tacky

indicators.note: in says the man's contraction goes inside the word for a club

parts.note: a dive is a seedy club
he's is short for the man is

explanation.surface: A man in a nightclub that is cheap and tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacky here means sticky, as glue or gum is.

clue.text: Tough newspaper editor threatened by severe competition

parts.note: tough means hard
the press is the newspaper industry

explanation.surface: A tough editor of a newspaper fighting off its rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under heavy pressure, as a firm squeezed by rivals, is a common sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Rowing crew beginning to hurry just a fraction

parts.note: an eight is a crew of eight rowers

indicators.note: beginning to selects the first letter of the word hurry

explanation.surface: A rowing crew starts to speed up, but only slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: One part in eight is a fraction, and 'just a' hints it is small.

clue.text: Family will go from mistaking terrible shame

indicators.note: will go from says the family letters are subtracted from the fodder
terrible suggests the remaining letters of mistaking are jumbled

parts.note: kin means family

explanation.surface: A family will leave after a terrible error, in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove KIN from MISTAKING and rearrange MISTAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace attached to someone.

clue.text: One's so covering miles in such a strip of land

parts.note: one is I, so one's gives I plus S

indicators.note: covering says the word for so wraps around the abbreviation for miles

parts.note: thus means so

explanation.surface: Someone describing a narrow piece of land that stretches for miles.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow neck of land joining two larger areas, like Panama or Suez, has this geographical name.

clue.text: Father has unusual items offering interest

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters of items are set in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Dad collects odd items, which makes for an engaging hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby or recreation is something one takes an interest in, so an interest can name it.

clue.text: Secretary hugging tree that was official in Turkey

indicators.note: hugging says the assistant's letters wrap around the tree

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant or secretary
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A secretary embracing a tree that once belonged to an Ottoman official.
explanation.definitionFit: A title for a high-ranking Ottoman governor or military commander.

clue.text: Caiaphas, perhaps — strangely he is right to keep quiet

indicators.note: to keep says the shuffled letters hold another letter inside them
strangely asks for the words he is right to be shuffled into an odd order

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quiet

explanation.surface: Someone oddly claims Caiaphas was right to stay silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' scrambles HE IS RIGHT, and 'to keep' puts P inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Caiaphas was the Jewish chief priest who presided at the trial of Jesus, an example of the title.

clue.text: Country post may see liberal moving to the west

indicators.note: in an across answer west is leftward, so this letter shifts towards the start

parts.note: post means mail

explanation.surface: Postal workers notice a liberal heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: The L in MAIL moves one place left, before the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked West African nation whose capital is Bamako.

clue.text: Lead, say in hard rock?

definitions.meaning: lead is an example of a dense element such as lead or mercury
a loud, aggressive form of rock music

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as a verb or a front position; here it is the metal. 'Hard rock' looks geological but is the music.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a dense toxic element, and the phrase also names a loud guitar-driven rock genre.

clue.text: Give way, leaving space deferentially

indicators.note: leaving says the letters we want are what is left inside the words space deferentially once the rest goes

explanation.surface: Someone yields politely, stepping aside with deference.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield or surrender ground, as when a country gives up territory.
